title: A KnowledgeUnit schema forces epistemic standing at every long-lived memory write
content:
## Claim

Any skill writing into a long-lived knowledge layer should emit operations against a `KnowledgeUnit` (or equivalent) document model whose state requires epistemic context at write time.

## Required standing

- `author` (human or agent)
- `producer` skill ref when agent-authored
- `epistemicMode` (OBSERVATION, INFERENCE, RETRIEVAL, SYNTHESIS, SPECULATION)
- optional `confidence`
- `sources` and `derivedFrom`
- `reviewStatus` and `scope`

## Payoff

The vault becomes queryable: everything I asserted; exclude low-confidence agent units; all units derived from skill X. The human/agent boundary stays legible after the session ends.

```graphql
type KnowledgeUnit {
  id: ID!
  claim: String!
  author: Actor!
  producer: SkillRef
  epistemicMode: EpistemicMode!
  confidence: Float
  sources: [Source!]!
  derivedFrom: [ID!]!
  reviewStatus: ReviewStatus!
  scope: Scope!
  createdAt: DateTime!
}
```

## Methodology grounding
The claims below live in the plugin's `data/methodology/` corpus; the relationship is stated per claim.

- **[[agent self-memory should be architecturally separate from user knowledge systems]]** — BUILDS_ON. The methodology claim separates an agent's working preferences from the research graph on the grounds that self-knowledge need not pass the composability test. A typed KnowledgeUnit is the mechanism that makes the boundary enforceable rather than conventional: the schema is what refuses an untyped write into the long-lived layer.
- **[[IBIS framework maps claim-based architecture to structured argumentation]]** — RELATES_TO. Both hold that a knowledge record's *kind* is load-bearing. IBIS types a contribution as issue, position or argument; a KnowledgeUnit types it by epistemic standing. Neither leaves the reader to infer status from prose.
description: Mandatory fields for author, producer skill, epistemic mode, confidence, sources, derivation, and review status keep vault contributions attributable.
